lines.en: I woke up this morning with a strange image in my head.
It’s me — alone in a cabbage patch, but each cabbage is colored with a different hue to match every single set of eyes I know.
There’s even one for mine — growing all by itself in a row ten meters detached from the rest, swarmed by flies and other insects as I’m the only one the farmers neglected to spray with deterrent.
Though, it seems more like they forgot me entirely given how beautiful the rest are.

Some are doing better than others. Like a blue one and a pink one. Which is impressive on its own as it seems their sunlight is blotted out by massive spheres of ruby and aquamarine that rule over the fields.
I know who these are for, of course — the two greatest loves I’ve ever had and the two who, if life was really fair, would grow even larger and feed me for all eternity.
This is not my farm, though. I am merely a man who presently sees it. The cabbage growing in the corner, if you will.
But if you won’t, I implore you to dig deep within yourself for a scythe made of doubt to hack up the rest of what’s grown or is growing while you leave me here to fend off the flies.
I am certain this vision must have meant something, as does my request to have you falsify it before I can double it and give it to the next person.

And no, this is no plea to “save everyone else and leave me here to rot” or something of that nature. In fact, it’s quite the opposite as I would very much like to continue living. At least for right now.
My guess at what this image means, though, is that I grow in different ways. That, by “fending off the flies,” what I’m really doing is living inversely.
Picture this — that they are not here to feed on my decaying matter or give birth to their children, but to pick me clean like I’ve become a termite queen myself.
Then, once the rotten bits are gone, I’ll be born again. The farmers will return and look down at me as their last bit of hope. Then they’ll chop me up and mix me with pork and make me into gyoza.
That’s the hope, at least. That’d give me purpose apart from making the other cabbages look more appetizing.
There’s probably something else, too. But you can check back at the end of the weekend once I’ve had some more time to think about it.
In the meantime, I’m going to keep plowing the fields of this forgotten farm in hopes of uncovering something either buried beneath my feet or hidden somewhere inside of my head.
It’d be really weird to just imagine an avant-garde cabbage patch for no reason after all.
Especially while I’m surrounded by a bunch of teenage girls in an inn roughly twelve hours before any other adults arrive.
I’m pretty sure it would make a lot more sense to just focus on them for now.
: And so marks the start of yet another Rooftop Apocalypse Squad slumber party meeting! A ritual that, despite being almost entirely unsuccessful, is still fun no matter what!

: Now, if we could please get a moment of silence for Uta and Tsuneyo who were not able to join us today, it’d be both greatly appreciated and an excellent start to what I’m sure will be a very brief and very weird meeting.
: You make it sound as if they died.
: I’m confused. Tsuneyo is a part of this group as well? I was not aware of this.
: Yeah, none of us really know what’s going on with her, to be honest. Sometimes she’s aware, sometimes she isn’t. So I just invite her to everything now to be safe.
: Seeing as a moment of silence is likely impossible in this group, I say we just move past your pseudo-eulogy and address the matter most dramatically at hand right now.
: You mean that your mom knows you’re gettin’ porked by the teacher and now thinks you’re crazy because she’s some kinda outlier?
: Damn. That sucks.
: It’s worse than when my dad died, honestly.
: How did your father die? I thought time was repeating itself.
: Maybe he’s dying every single reset loop? And I’m allowed to say that without sounding like a bitch since that’s exactly what’s probably going on with my mom from now on. Still kinda TBD on that.
: Right, which is why we should spend the rest of the night planning out how to murder her so we can answer this question once and for all.
: No, Makoto. We are not going to spend the night planning how to kill your mother. Parents are hard to come by in 1-A and we can’t just be getting rid of them whenever they inconvenience us.
: Easy for you to say. Both of your parents are basically unaware of your existence while my only remaining one is too aware.
: This is what happens when it takes too long for shame to first reach a person. Makoto is ill-prepared to have other people know she’s having sex.
: There won’t be anything to be ashamed of anymore once I am a murderer.
: No murder. Bad Makoto. What we need to be doing right now is figuring out how to get your mom to join the apocalypse squad, not be excommunicated from the planet.
: Join?! Absolutely not! What can she possibly contribute to any of this?!
: Yumi doesn’t really contribute either and we’ve never tried to kill her.
: She did try to kill me, though.
: Yeah, and I’d be trying it again right now if Ponytail weren’t in the fucking way.
: Oh, good. Now I can’t get up for another drink without becoming an accomplice to murder. Slumber parties are so much fun.
: Can we at least wait until after the next reset to...you know...include her? Like, there’s a very real chance she gets sent back and we never have to deal with any of this again, right?
: Do you know when this next “reset” is, exactly? Is there a specific date it usually occurs on? Any signs to look out for beforehand?
: Not really. I feel like one needs to be coming up soon, though. Our last one spat us out in Christmalloween and that was like a whole nine months ago.
: And “Christmalloween” is not actually a holiday in the correct timeline, yes? It’s a product of time unraveling or something of that nature.
: Right.
: No. Not right. Christmalloween is real and Ayane is lying to you. And you can definitely trust me because I’m the real Maya who was never reset or anything like that.

: Mhm, right. So you’ve just been acting like a brand new Maya ever since the first one disappeared and broke Sensei in half? And you are only revealing this now because of how important it is to preserve Christmalloween?

: That’s right. Everything from the moment of my “disappearance” up until now was all a clever ploy to make Sensei fall in love with me again. And now that I have succeeded, there is no reason to keep it up.
: How come everybody in this fuckin’ class thinks that guy is in love with them?
: You don’t need to say “that guy,” Yumi. I’m right here.
: Cool, yeah. I’ll just ask you then. Why do all these morons think you’re in love with them when you’re really just a serial rapist?
: I imagine it’s a mix of boredom, lack of options, persistence, hope, competitive nature, my unrivaled manliness and remarkably good looks.
: That’s a lot of words to say they’re all just fuckin’ stupid.

: I agree, Yumi. It is quite obvious that Sensei is in love with me and me only and that everyone else has merely fallen victim to his charm, unrivaled manliness, and remarkably good looks. But I digress.
: You can’t digress after a blatant lie like that! If anything, Maya is the one he really loves here.
: See? Even Makoto knows.
: Regardless of who loves who or why Christmalloween is fake or any other tangential thingy we’re almost getting sidetracked by, we came here for a reason and that reason is to make progress.
: Makoto, if your mom really is aware now, we can’t just ignore her. Try thinking of it as an opportunity to have her support your relationship or something. I saw your PowerPoint. I was convinced.
: And the unfortunate truth is that if she experiences even a fragment of what we have, who you’re sleeping with will be the least of her worries.
: Somehow I doubt that...But still, I think we should at least wait until-
: Yes. We’ll wait until after the next reset to indoctrinate her. I doubt anything else would be able to convince her this is legitimate anyway.
: That it for the meeting then? We done?
: Not quite. There are still a few other matters we need to address. Sensei?
: Ayane and I “woke up” with what seems like some sort of...shared memory or something after the last reset. But we don’t know how or why we wound up with it.
: The “memory” Sensei is referring to, if we’re going to call it that, is that Maya may or may not be the cause of this for some reason.
: Interesting.
: Bullshit is more like it. I think I’d know if I were God.
: Not exactly. And especially not if you’re a different person now from the one you were in the beginning.
: Don’t encourage them. This is annoying enough without a smart person on their team.
: Oh, well fuck me I guess. How exactly are we even supposed to investigate such a thing, though? Because it’s not as if we can trace Maya’s past when none of it is in the files.
: That’s what the meeting’s for, Makoto! It’s not just Maya we need to “investigate,” though. It’s Ami too.
: Ami?
: She’s been acting weird for a while now. Very weird. And Maya will vouch for that. Right, Maya?
: Uh...y...yeah.
: Yeah, she’s...weird.
: Interesting. I wonder if this has anything to do with her going through all of my things the other day? Does she know I’ve gained knowledge of all this yet?
: She probably just smelled a lingering trace of Sensei on your belongings and wanted to check if he was inside of them.
: Now, this is Ami we're talking about. So she's always going to have some bit of weirdness to her no matter what we do and I'm sure she has her reasons for that.
: So I'm not suggesting we bombard her with questions or invite her to these meetings or anything of that nature- but that we simply be wary of her. That's all.
: That was the method pre-reset Maya took, and I'm confident now that she did that for a reason. Even if pre-reset Maya was wrong like 75%% of the time.
: And I...still don’t think she’s involved.
: Yes, and you can keep thinking that since I don’t want you breaking down again in the event that she is. You can leave her to us, Sensei. You just keep treating her the way you always do.
: Or you can just man up and deal with the fact that sometimes, the people in your life ain’t what you thought they’d be.
: Oh, thank you for picking now to contribute, Yumi. What excellent timing for such helpful advice.
: I’m just sayin’, if the two of you guys really want to put an end to all of this shit like you’ve been ranting about nonstop lately, the fuck is babying each other when shit gets hard gonna do?
: Say that incestuous weirdo does know something. Say she’s somehow the key to fuckin’ all of this...
: Is Sensei just gonna hide in his room again while a bunch of stupid teenagers try to put the fucking world as we know it back together? Or is he gonna fucking do something about it?
: Is there any reason for this sudden hostility or are you just hungry again?
: Just thinkin’ out loud.

: I don’t know shit about Ponytail or the fucking genius over there, but Four Eyes and I don’t really mind stayin’ trapped here. So why should we be doin’ all the work for the two people who do want to leave?
: I don’t wanna help somebody who ain’t gonna try to help themself. So you can keep all that Ami shit away from me. The less I need to talk to her, the better.
: I mean...yeah. That's kind of the point I was getting at.
: I, too, find the idea of infinity quite appealing, if anyone would like my opinion.
: Fuck you, cunt. Get your own fucking opinion. That one’s mine.
: Why do you want to leave, if I may ask? What is there to gain from a more real version of reality?
: Well, I...
: You see, we...uh...
: There’s something waiting for us outside of this place.
: I don’t really know what it is and...I don’t think Ayane really knows either, but...
: Whatever it is, I don’t think we’re going to find here.
: Akira...
: Yumi is right about my attitude toward Ami. I need to stop being a coward and I shouldn’t rely on any of you to fight my battles for me.
: I’ll talk to her. I just...have to find the right time.
: Aight, well if Blondie’s just gonna stand there lookin’ all proud and in love and shit, I’m gonna go take a walk and try not to throw up.
: No, no. It’s fine.
: We came to the beach a full day early to try and get each other up to speed, sure. But these meetings are more about just being together than actually getting anything done.
: As an FYI, Nodoka, she’s only saying that because we never get anything done.
: Thank you. I was unsure if the lackadaisical approach was the norm or if we were just abstaining from feasible progress on account of Uta’s absence.
: It’s the norm. This RSA shit is like 99%% planning and then waiting around for the world to do something before we can.
: Again, this is more about just being together than actually-
: Yeah, I’m gonna go for a walk now. Nice meeting, y’all.
: Okay. Well, I guess I’ll just sit down too then.
: You think Sensei’s going to be okay talking to Ami?
: Only one way to find out. Seems more feasible than you talking to your mom at this point.
: Well, yes. Ami doesn’t hold Sensei to the highest standard possible and my mother would rather me stay abstinent for thousands of years than sleep with someone her age.
: There is not nearly enough food here.
: That’s your seventh pizza.
: I said what I said and I stand by it.
: Yumi, may I speak to you for a moment?
: No. You may not.
: Oh.
: Then, may I speak in your general direction and assume that you hear?
: The fuck do you want, Nodoka?
: In hindsight, I believe stealing your clothes and commanding you to masturbate in the locker room may have been a mean thing to do.
: And?
: And I acknowledge that I was most likely in the wrong there.
: This an apology?
: I’ll apologize to you when you apologize to Futaba for making her doubt herself more than she already does.
: I did apologize to her, you fucking-
: If merely saying the words “I’m sorry” was enough to make an apology sincere, I would have no trouble at all doing the same right now.
: But I have learned recently that it is not. And that these things must come from a place somewhere in close proximity to one’s chest cavity in order to come across as “real.”
: You aren’t sorry for the things you said to Futaba. You still belittle her. You just do it behind her back now.
: Yeah, but I never fucking commanded her to masturbate in a locker room.
: Perhaps not. But you have stolen her clothes. And had her parade herself around the showers looking for something to cover herself with like she has something to be ashamed of when she doesn’t.
: I’ve heard the stories. Of the things you’ve done to torment her despite her doing nothing to you whatsoever. But I do not understand them as good antagonists typically come with a motive.
: I have seen the way she cries and heard the shaking of her voice as the shame pours from out her mouth. But as I repeat these words to you, you stand there unchanged and unrepentant.
: Is it that you take joy in hurting people? And merely picked the lowest hanging fruit you could? Or was there something else you were hoping to gain from breaking her?
: Will you ever be sorry?
: Will you, Nodoka?
: Can machines even feel in the first place?
: I am trying.
: That’s why I am here.
: Well...maybe that’s why I’m here too.
: Okay. Well, goodbye then, I suppose.
